verdict.rationale: Smithery documents a dedicated per-server page where users can discover and try a server. It also scans servers for metadata, with a static server card as fallback, and distinguishes local stdio bundles from URL-published remote servers. That implies tool and hosting info is surfaced, but the evidence never shows a pre-connection view of input schemas, transport, or hosting attributes, and the CLI/API was shut down while only the public registry remains. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that listings expose tool input schemas, transport type and hosting attributes before connecting; current-state evidence of the inspection surface after the shutdown; hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can inspect a listed server's tools, input schemas, transport, and hosting attributes before connecting to it

citations.quote: Get a dedicated server page where users can discover, try, and install your MCP from any client
If automatic scanning can’t complete (auth wall, required configuration, or other issues), you can provide server metadata manually via a static server card at `/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json`
For local stdio servers — Smithery distributes a pre-built MCPB bundle that clients download and run locally.
Smithery will remain as a public (non-proxied) MCP registry.
